:::{#thm-moore-penrose-eigendecomposition}
#### The Moore-Penrose inverse of a symmetric matrix from its eigendecomposition

Let $\matr{S} = \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\tp{\matr{Q}}$ be an eigendecomposition (@def-eigendecomposition) of a [symmetric matrix](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix) $\matr{S}$,
with [diagonal entries](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-diagonal-entry) $\eigval_1, \ldots, \eigval_p$ in the [diagonal matrix](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-diagonal-matrix) $\matr{\Eigvals}$.
Let $\matr{\Eigvals}^+$ be the diagonal matrix with $j$th [diagonal entry](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-diagonal-entry) $1/\eigval_j$ if $\eigval_j \ne 0$ and $0$ if $\eigval_j = 0$.
Then

$$
\matr{S}^+ = \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}.
$$

:::

::: proof

Let $\matr{G} = \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}$.
By @thm-moore-penrose-unique, it is enough to show that $\matr{G}$ satisfies the four conditions of @def-moore-penrose for $\matr{S}$.

**Two facts about the diagonal matrices.**
The $j$th [diagonal entry](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-diagonal-entry) of $\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals}$ is $\eigval_j \cdot (1/\eigval_j) \cdot \eigval_j = \eigval_j$ if $\eigval_j \ne 0$, and $0 = \eigval_j$ if $\eigval_j = 0$.
So $\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals} = \matr{\Eigvals}$.
In the same way, $\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+ = \matr{\Eigvals}^+$.
Both $\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+$ and $\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals}$ are diagonal, so each is [symmetric](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix).

**Conditions 1 and 2.**

$$
\ba
\matr{S}\matr{G}\matr{S}
&= \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\tp{\matr{Q}}\,\matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}\,\matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\tp{\matr{Q}}
&& \text{(definitions of } \matr{S} \text{ and } \matr{G} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals}\tp{\matr{Q}}
&& (\tp{\matr{Q}}\matr{Q} = \matr{I}, \text{ twice})
\\
&= \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\tp{\matr{Q}}
&& (\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals} = \matr{\Eigvals})
\\
&= \matr{S},
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{S} \text{)}
\ea
$$

and likewise

$$
\ba
\matr{G}\matr{S}\matr{G}
&= \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}
&& (\tp{\matr{Q}}\matr{Q} = \matr{I}, \text{ twice})
\\
&= \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}
&& (\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+ = \matr{\Eigvals}^+)
\\
&= \matr{G}.
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{G} \text{)}
\ea
$$

**Conditions 3 and 4.**

$$
\ba
\matr{S}\matr{G}
&= \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}
&& (\tp{\matr{Q}}\matr{Q} = \matr{I})
\\
&= \tp{\paren{\matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}}}
&& (\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+ \text{ is diagonal, so equals its transpose})
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{S}\matr{G})},
&& \text{(just shown, in the other order)}
\ea
$$

and the same steps with $\matr{\Eigvals}^+\matr{\Eigvals}$ in place of $\matr{\Eigvals}\matr{\Eigvals}^+$ give $\matr{G}\matr{S} = \tp{(\matr{G}\matr{S})}$.

:::
